issues.problem: 'आकर' (having come) is not in the Sanskrit; upa is only the preverb 'near' (English keeps 'near to').
issues.fix: हे मनुष्यो, इस शुद्ध होती हुई बूँद के लिए पास गाओ; वह देवगणों तक पहुँचना चाहता है।

issues.problem: hita after hinvānaḥ hetṛbhiḥ is most naturally the pp. of √hi 'impel' (the same root as hinvāna and hetṛ), not √dhā 'set in place'; Hindi 'स्थापित' and English 'set in place' follow the weaker option. Decide: keep and note the alternative, or change to 'sent forth' / 'भेजा हुआ'.
issues.fix: gloss: sent forth, impelled; gram: m. nom. sg. pp. √hi (or √dhā); English 'Urged on by the impellers, sent forth, the racer has stepped to the prize'

issues.problem: -masi is the primary ACTIVE ending of the 1 pl.; the middle would be -mahe. 'mid.' is wrong.
Gloss and Hindi say 'worthy of fame' (śravāyya, gdv.); 'famed' is a different sense and the two layers disagree.
issues.fix: You, O god, bestow on us wide, worthy of fame, great good heroism, O Agni.

issues.where: ब्रह्म से जुते हुए, केशों वाले
issues.problem: Glossary: brahman (n.) = sacred word (पवित्र वचन); bare 'ब्रह्म' reads as the god/absolute and disagrees with the English 'sacred word'. 'केशों वाले' (having hairs) is also weaker than the English 'long-maned'.
issues.fix: हे इन्द्र, पवित्र वचन से जुते हुए, लम्बे अयाल वाले दो भूरे घोड़े तुम्हें यहाँ लाएँ; हमारे पवित्र वचनों को सुनो।

patch.old: ब्रह्म से जुते हुए, केशों वाले
patch.new: पवित्र वचन से जुते हुए, लम्बे अयाल वाले

issues.problem: Gloss says 'yoke-fellows' (plural) for a singular instrumental.
-tām is the ACTIVE 3 du. imperative ending (middle would be -ātām/-etām); 'mid.' is wrong.

issues.where: being in heaven, I take on earth
issues.problem: Layers contradict the word analysis: sat is glossed n. nom. sg. (agreeing with jātam, 'birth being in heaven'), but both translations attach it to 'I' (masc.) as 'being in heaven, I take'. Either gram or translations must change; the construction is uncertain, so a human should pick.
issues.fix: Option A (follow gram): English 'On high is your birth, of the juice, being in heaven; I take on earth mighty shelter, great fame.' Hindi 'ऊँचा है तुम्हारा जन्म, रस का, जो आकाश में है; मैं पृथ्वी पर उग्र शरण, महान कीर्ति ग्रहण करता हूँ।' Option B: keep translations and change gram of sat to a subject-neutral label; add a note.

issues.problem: Same verb root √van/√san (win) in both English renderings ('wishing to win ... may we win'); Hindi switches to 'प्राप्त करें', so the layers do not match.
issues.fix: इससे, हे स्वामी, मनुष्यों के सब द्युम्न जीतने की इच्छा करते हुए हम जीतें।

issues.problem: Hindi 'took/grasped' disagrees with English 'has settled on' (ā-√sad 'sit upon'); the Hindi also changes the verb's sense.
issues.fix: वह प्राचीन साझा स्थान पर बैठ गया है

patch.new: वह प्राचीन साझा स्थान पर बैठ गया है

issues.where: Like a horse, a racer, cleansing you
issues.problem: Ambiguous: vājinam agrees with tvā (you, the racer), as the notes say, but 'Like a horse, a racer, cleansing you' reads as if the racer were a second comparison or the subject. Same in Hindi.
issues.fix: Cleansing you, the racer, like a horse, they lead you toward the sacred grass with reins.

patch.new: Cleansing you, the racer, like a horse, they lead you toward the sacred grass with reins.

summary: Draft is generally sound: tokens, glossary renderings and the [unclear] handling in 655, 669, 671 are correct, Hindi has no Latin letters/brackets/parentheses, and the single text_flag (657 asṛkṣata) is reasonable. 3 errors (667 brahman rendered as bare ब्रह्म in Hindi; 672 sat attached to 'I' against its own gram; 676 Hindi/English verb disagreement) and 9 minor (wrong active/middle labels in 661 and 671, 651 added 'आकर', 655 hita root, 662/668/674/677/678 consistency). No regrouping suggested. Manual decisions: 672 (construction of divi sat), 655 (hita root). Unit 672 may be a copy variant of the RV parallel (sad vs ṣad) but this was not verified, so no text_flag is proposed.
